+# Papel real via SET LOCAL ROLE em transacao (a escrita persiste; papel+claims valem no bloco).
+as_auth() {
+  local uid="$1" sql="$2"
+  local jwt="{\"sub\":\"$uid\"}"
+  docker exec "$container_name" psql -X -qAt -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -U postgres -d postgres \
+    -c "BEGIN; SET LOCAL ROLE authenticated; SELECT set_config('request.jwt.claims', '$jwt', false); $sql; COMMIT;"
+}
+as_anon() {
+  local sql="$1"
+  docker exec "$container_name" psql -X -qAt -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -U postgres -d postgres \
+    -c "BEGIN; SET LOCAL ROLE anon; $sql; COMMIT;"
+}
+expect_line_as() { # label expected uid sql ‚Äî passa se expected for UMA linha cheia da saida
+  local l="$1" e="$2" j="$3" s="$4" out
+  out="$(as_auth "$j" "$s")"
+  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qxF "$e" || { printf '%s\n' "$out" >&2; fail "$l: esperado linha '$e'"; }
+  pass "$l"
+}
+expect_error_as() { # label needle uid sql
+  local l="$1" needle="$2" j="$3" s="$4" out st
+  set +e; out="$(as_auth "$j" "$s" 2>&1)"; st=$?; set -e
+  (( st == 0 )) && { printf '%s\n' "$out" >&2; fail "$l: deveria falhar, mas passou"; }
+  [[ "$out" == *"$needle"* ]] || { printf '%s\n' "$out" >&2; fail "$l: esperava '$needle' no erro"; }
+  pass "$l"
+}
+expect_error_anon() { # label needle sql
+  local l="$1" needle="$2" s="$3" out st
+  set +e; out="$(as_anon "$s" 2>&1)"; st=$?; set -e
+  (( st == 0 )) && { printf '%s\n' "$out" >&2; fail "$l: deveria falhar, mas passou"; }
+  [[ "$out" == *"$needle"* ]] || { printf '%s\n' "$out" >&2; fail "$l: esperava '$needle' no erro"; }
+  pass "$l"
+}
+expect_error_sql() { # label needle sql (como postgres ‚Äî sondagem de CHECK)
+  local l="$1" needle="$2" s="$3" out st
+  set +e; out="$(psql_sql "$s" 2>&1)"; st=$?; set -e
+  (( st == 0 )) && { printf '%s\n' "$out" >&2; fail "$l: deveria falhar, mas passou"; }
+  [[ "$out" == *"$needle"* ]] || { printf '%s\n' "$out" >&2; fail "$l: esperava '$needle' no erro"; }
+  pass "$l"
+}

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# R2-DB-023 (item 304 / #304, P2) ‚Äî "Trigger de recuperacao ainda escreve campo removido e bloqueia
+# o pedido autenticado" (docs/reconciliation/reaudit/2026-10-03/reports/database/findings.json,
+# achado R2-DB-023; consumidor src/pages/ForgotPassword.tsx).
+#
+# Roda o MESMO roteiro no mesmo container descartavel, em dois blocos:
+#   BLOCO A ‚Äî estado ANTERIOR (defeito), montado em pre.sql a partir do canonico:
+#             a coluna reset_token ja NAO existe (20260411111454), mas o gatilho BEFORE INSERT
+#             public.sanitize_reset_request_trigger continua vivo e o corpo vencedor de
+#             public.sanitize_reset_request() (20260410103156) escreve `NEW.reset_token := NULL`
+#             quando auth.uid() existe. O plpgsql levanta `record "new" has no field "reset_token"`
+#             ANTES de gravar: o INSERT autenticado morre ‚Äî inclusive o do usuario LOGADO
+#             (payload valido, email do proprio usuario, permitido pela policy de INSERT).
+#   BLOCO B ‚Äî migration real aplicada sobre esse estado: o corpo novo nao cita a coluna removida;
+#             o pedido do usuario autenticado passa a persistir como 'pending' e com os campos de
+#             revisao/token sempre saneados; o rate limit canonico segue valendo; a funcao continua
+#             sem EXECUTE para anon/authenticated; e o caminho sem sessao segue devolvendo NEW como
+#             antes, sem lookup em auth.users nem canonicalizacao de email.
+
+set -Eeuo pipefail
+
+repo_root="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
+migration="${RESET_GATILHO_MIGRATION:-$repo_root/supabase/migrations/20261006231105_recuperacao_gatilho_sem_coluna_removida.sql}"
+postgres_image="${RESET_GATILHO_TEST_POSTGRES_IMAGE:-postgres:17-alpine}"
+container_name="zapp-v2-reset-gatilho-test-$$"
+
+cleanup() {
+  if [[ "$container_name" =~ ^zapp-v2-reset-gatilho-test-[0-9]+$ ]]; then
+    docker rm -f "$container_name" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+  fi
+}
+trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM
+
+fail() { printf '[FAIL] %s\n' "$1" >&2; exit 1; }
+
+psql_sql() {
+  docker exec "$container_name" psql -X -qAt -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -U postgres -d postgres -c "$1"
+}
+psql_file() {
+  docker exec -i "$container_name" psql -X -qAt -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -U postgres -d postgres < "$1"
+}
+as_role() {  # as_role <papel> <jwt|-> <sql>
+  local role="$1" jwt="$2" sql="$3" claims
+  if [[ "$jwt" == "-" ]]; then claims=""; else claims="SELECT set_config('request.jwt.claims', '$jwt', false);"; fi
+  docker exec "$container_name" psql -X -qAt -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -U postgres -d postgres \
+    -c "SET ROLE $role; $claims $sql"
+}
+expect_value() {
+  local l="$1" e="$2" s="$3" a
+  a="$(psql_sql "$s" | tail -n1)"
+  [[ "$a" == "$e" ]] || fail "$l: esperado '$e', obtido '$a'"
+  printf '[PASS] %s\n' "$l"
+}
+expect_value_as() {
+  local l="$1" e="$2" r="$3" j="$4" s="$5" a
+  a="$(as_role "$r" "$j" "$s" | tail -n1)"
+  [[ "$a" == "$e" ]] || fail "$l: esperado '$e', obtido '$a'"
+  printf '[PASS] %s\n' "$l"
+}
+expect_error_as() {
+  local l="$1" needle="$2" r="$3" j="$4" s="$5" out st
+  set +e; out="$(as_role "$r" "$j" "$s" 2>&1)"; st=$?; set -e
+  (( st == 0 )) && { printf '%s\n' "$out" >&2; fail "$l: deveria falhar, mas passou"; }
+  [[ "$out" == *"$needle"* ]] || { printf '%s\n' "$out" >&2; fail "$l: esperava '$needle' no erro"; }
+  printf '[PASS] %s\n' "$l"
+}
+expect_ok_as() {
+  local l="$1" r="$2" j="$3" s="$4"
+  as_role "$r" "$j" "$s" >/dev/null || fail "$l: deveria ter sucesso ($r)"
+  printf '[PASS] %s\n' "$l"
+}

+command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail 'python3 nao esta instalado'
+docker info >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail 'Docker daemon nao esta acessivel'
+[[ -f "$migration" ]] || fail "migration nao encontrada: $migration"

+  sleep 1

+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+src, dst = map(Path, sys.argv[1:3])
+rollback = []
+capturing = False
+for line in src.read_text(encoding='utf-8').splitlines():
+    if line.startswith('--     CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION'):

+    raise SystemExit('bloco Rollback executavel nao encontrado na migration')

+function validarFlags(tokens, origem) {
+  if (tokens.length === 0) throw new Error(`contrato ${origem}: chamada sem flags de cliente`);
+  const juntos = tokens.join(' ');
+  if (!/(^|\s)-v\s+ON_ERROR_STOP=1(\s|$)/.test(juntos)) {
+    throw new Error(`contrato ${origem}: falta -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 (o SQL falharia em silencio)`);
+  }
+  for (const token of tokens) {
+    if (!FLAGS_ACEITOS.has(token)) {
+      throw new Error(`contrato ${origem}: flag nao declarada "${token}"`);
+    }
+  }
+  return tokens;

+// O corpo de -c "..." e uma string bash entre aspas duplas, nao SQL literal:
+// dentro dela o bash desfaz apenas \" \\ \$ \` e \<newline> (continuacao de
+// linha) e EXPANDE $VAR, $(...), ${...}, `...`. UMA passada caractere a
+// caractere reproduz o que o bash entrega ao psql e recusa (fail-closed) o que
+// ele reinterpretaria: expansao, crase solta e barra invertida fora dos 4
+// escapes. O `$` e examinado no texto BRUTO: `\$` e literal para o bash.
+export function desfazerAspasDuplasBash(corpo, origem) {
+  const texto = String(corpo);
+  const saida = [];
+  for (let i = 0; i < texto.length; i += 1) {
+    const c = texto[i];
+    if (c === '\\') {
+      const proximo = texto[i + 1];
+      if (proximo === '"' || proximo === '\\' || proximo === '$' || proximo === '`') {
+        saida.push(proximo);
+        i += 1;
+        continue;
+      }
+      if (proximo === '\n') {
+        i += 1; // continuacao de linha do bash: os dois somem
+        continue;
+      }
+      throw new Error(
+        `contrato ${origem}: -c " tem barra invertida que o bash nao trata como escape ("\\${proximo ?? ''}")`,
+      );
+    }
+    if (c === '`') {
+      throw new Error(`contrato ${origem}: o texto de -c tem substituicao de shell (crase); nao e SQL`);
+    }
+    if (c === '$' && /[A-Za-z0-9_$@*#?!({\[-]/.test(texto[i + 1] ?? '')) {
+      throw new Error(
+        `contrato ${origem}: o texto de -c tem substituicao de shell ("$${texto[i + 1]}..."); nao e SQL`,
+      );
+    }
+    saida.push(c);
+  }
+  return saida.join('');
+}

+function validarSql(sql, origem) {
+  const texto = desfazerAspasDuplasBash(sql, origem).trim();
+  if (!texto) throw new Error(`contrato ${origem}: -c sem SQL`);
+  if (/RUNTIME=/.test(texto)) {
+    throw new Error(`contrato ${origem}: o texto de -c tem substituicao de shell; nao e SQL`);
+  }
+  if (!/^(WITH|SELECT|VALUES)\b/i.test(texto)) {
+    throw new Error(`contrato ${origem}: o texto de -c nao comeca por WITH/SELECT/VALUES`);
+  }
+  return texto;

+/**
+ * Le um contrato declarado e devolve as invocacoes que ele declara, na ordem.
+ * Cada invocacao: { versoes: string[]|null, generico: boolean, flags: string[],
+ *                   sql: string|null, arquivo: string|null, script: string }.
+ * `versoes` e null apenas no ramo generico (`*)`).

+export function extrairInvocacoes(texto, versaoDoArquivo, origem = '<contrato>') {
+  const linhas = String(texto).split('\n');
+  const invocacoes = [];
+  let rotulo = null;
+  let rotuloPendente = false;
+  let primeira = true;
+
+  for (let i = 0; i < linhas.length; i += 1) {
+    const casouRotulo = ROTULO.exec(linhas[i]);
+    if (casouRotulo) {
+      rotulo = casouRotulo[1] ? casouRotulo[1].split('|') : null;
+      rotuloPendente = true;
+      continue;
+    }
+    const chamada = CHAMADA.exec(linhas[i]);
+    if (!chamada) continue;
+
+    const script = chamada[1];
+    const resto = chamada[2];
+    let flags;
+    let sql = null;
+    let arquivo = null;
+
+    const inline = /^(.*?)-c\s+"\s*$/.exec(resto);
+    if (inline) {
+      flags = inline[1].trim();
+      const corpo = [];
+      let j = i + 1;
+      for (; j < linhas.length; j += 1) {
+        const fecha = /^([\s\S]*)"\)\s*$/.exec(linhas[j]);
+        if (fecha) {
+          corpo.push(fecha[1]);
+          break;
+        }
+        corpo.push(linhas[j]);
+      }
+      if (j >= linhas.length) {
+        throw new Error(`contrato ${origem}: -c " sem fechamento )\"`);
+      }
+      sql = validarSql(corpo.join('\n'), origem);
+      i = j;
+    } else if (/\\\s*$/.test(resto)) {
+      flags = resto.replace(/\\\s*$/, '').trim();
+      const continuacao = linhas[i + 1] ?? '';
+      const usaArquivo = /^\s*-f\s+(\S+)\)\s*$/.exec(continuacao);
+      if (!usaArquivo) {
+        throw new Error(`contrato ${origem}: continuacao sem "-f <arquivo>)"`);
+      }
+      arquivo = usaArquivo[1];
+      if (!/\.sql$/.test(arquivo)) {
+        throw new Error(`contrato ${origem}: arquivo de contrato nao termina em .sql ("${arquivo}")`);
+      }
+      i += 1;
+    } else {
+      throw new Error(
+        `contrato ${origem}: forma nao declarada em "${linhas[i].trim()}" (espere -c "<sql>" ou -f <arquivo>)`,
+      );
+    }

+    let versoes;
+    if (rotuloPendente) {

+    } else if (primeira) {

+    } else {
+      throw new Error(`contrato ${origem}: invocacao sem rotulo do case nem versao no nome do arquivo`);
+    }

+    invocacoes.push({ versoes, generico: rotuloPendente && rotulo === null, flags: flagsValidos, sql, arquivo, script });
+    primeira = false;
+    rotuloPendente = false;
+    rotulo = null;
+  }
+
+  return invocacoes;

+/** Mapa versao -> invocacao dedicada + a invocacao do ramo generico (`*)`). */
+export function invocacoesDosContratos(dir = CONTRATOS) {
+  const mapa = new Map();
+  let generico = null;
+  const arquivos = readdirSync(dir).filter((f) => /^\d{14}\.sql$/.test(f)).sort();
+  if (arquivos.length === 0) throw new Error(`nenhum contrato de runtime em ${dir}`);
+
+  for (const arquivo of arquivos) {
+    const versao = arquivo.replace(/\.sql$/, '');
+    const texto = readFileSync(join(dir, arquivo), 'utf8');
+    const invocacoes = extrairInvocacoes(texto, versao, arquivo);
+    if (invocacoes.length === 0) {
+      throw new Error(`contrato ${arquivo}: nenhuma invocacao declarada`);
+    }
+    for (const invocacao of invocacoes) {
+      if (invocacao.generico) {
+        if (generico) throw new Error('contrato: mais de um ramo generico (*) declarado');
+        generico = invocacao;
+        continue;
+      }
+      for (const v of invocacao.versoes) {
+        if (mapa.has(v)) throw new Error(`contrato: a versao ${v} esta declarada em mais de um contrato`);
+        mapa.set(v, invocacao);
+      }
+    }
+  }
+
+  if (!generico) {
+    throw new Error('contrato: nenhum ramo generico (*) declarado (nao ha fallback para o inventario)');
+  }
+  return { mapa, generico };
+}

+/**
+ * Invocacao que atende a versao alvo: a dedicada, se declarada; senao o contrato
+ * generico (com `generico: true`). Formato da versao invalido aborta.

+export function resolverInvocacao(versao, dir = CONTRATOS) {
+  const v = String(versao ?? '').trim();

+    throw new Error(`versao alvo invalida: "${versao}" (esperado 14 digitos)`);
+  }
+  const { mapa, generico } = invocacoesDosContratos(dir);
+  if (mapa.has(v)) return { ...mapa.get(v), generico: false };
+  return { ...generico, generico: true };
+}

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# N-141: as 9 policies de snooze/favorite/pin criadas pela 20260924230500 sem
+# clausula TO (vale para PUBLIC) passam a TO authenticated.
+#
+# BLOCO A (antes): aplica as MIGRATIONS REAIS (policies de apoio da 20260409 +
+#   a 20260924230500 inteira) e comprova o diagnostico: lista completa das 9
+#   policies TO public + anon com claims forjadas da dona explorando cada
+#   porta (GRAVA snooze ‚Äî unico comando TO public em snoozes ‚Äî e LE
+#   favorito/pin) ‚Äî nenhuma policy e recriada a mao neste script.
+# BLOCO B (depois): aplica a migration nova e prova: 0 {public}, as 9 nomeadas
+#   como {authenticated}, anon forjado ve 0 e o dono continua lendo e gravando
+#   (inclusive SELECT em snoozes, pela policy de apoio TO authenticated).
+# BLOCO C (rollback): extrai as linhas `--   ` do proprio arquivo da
+#   migration (mecanico, sem reescrever), executa, prova que voltou a {public}
+#   com a falha reaberta, e reaplica a migration (idempotencia).
+#
+# Vermelho: SKIP_MIGRATION=1 (simula a base sem a correcao) falha no B1;
+# numa worktree da base o arquivo da migration nem existe e o script aborta.
+
+set -Eeuo pipefail
+
+repo_root="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
+origin_base="$repo_root/supabase/migrations/20260409014536_3a836b4b-1e37-411c-b8af-45d918304272.sql"
+origin_idor="$repo_root/supabase/migrations/20260924230500_fix_contact_id_idor_snoozes_pins_favorites.sql"
+migration="$repo_root/supabase/migrations/20261011003011_scope_snoozes_pins_favorites_policies_to_authenticated.sql"
+postgres_image="${SNOOZES_TEST_POSTGRES_IMAGE:-postgres:17-alpine}"
+container_name="zapp-v2-snoozes-test-$$"
+
+cleanup() {
+  if [[ "$container_name" =~ ^zapp-v2-snoozes-test-[0-9]+$ ]]; then
+    docker rm -f "$container_name" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+  fi
+}
+trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM
+
+fail() { printf '[FAIL] %s\n' "$1" >&2; exit 1; }
+
+psql_sql() { docker exec "$container_name" psql -X -qAt -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -U postgres -d postgres -c "$1"; }
+psql_file() { docker exec -i "$container_name" psql -X -qAt -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -U postgres -d postgres < "$1"; }
+
+expect_value() {
+  local label="$1" expected="$2" sql="$3" actual
+  actual="$(psql_sql "$sql" | tail -n1)"
+  [[ "$actual" == "$expected" ]] || fail "$label: esperado '$expected', obtido '$actual'"
+  printf '[PASS] %s\n' "$label"
+}
+expect_ok() {
+  local l="$1" s="$2"
+  psql_sql "$s" >/dev/null || fail "$l: deveria ter sucesso"
+  printf '[PASS] %s\n' "$l"
+}
+
+command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail 'Docker nao esta instalado'
+docker info >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail 'Docker daemon nao esta acessivel'
+[[ -f "$origin_base" ]] || fail "origem nao encontrada: $origin_base"
+[[ -f "$origin_idor" ]] || fail "origem nao encontrada: $origin_idor"
+[[ -f "$migration" ]] || fail "migration nao encontrada: $migration"
+
+docker run --rm -d --name "$container_name" -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=test_only "$postgres_image" >/dev/null
+
+ready_checks=0
+for _ in $(seq 1 90); do
+  if psql_sql 'SELECT 1' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    ready_checks=$((ready_checks + 1)); (( ready_checks >= 2 )) && break
+  else ready_checks=0; fi
+  sleep 1
+done
+(( ready_checks >= 2 )) || fail 'PostgreSQL descartavel nao ficou pronto'
+
+tmp_dir="$(mktemp -d)"
+trap 'rm -rf "$tmp_dir"; cleanup' EXIT INT TERM
+
+# Andaime: so tabelas/papeis/concessoes. NENHUMA policy aqui.
+cat > "$tmp_dir/pre.sql" <<'SQL'
+CREATE ROLE anon NOLOGIN;
+CREATE ROLE authenticated NOLOGIN;
+
+CREATE SCHEMA auth;
+CREATE FUNCTION auth.uid() RETURNS uuid LANGUAGE sql STABLE
+  AS $$ SELECT nullif(coalesce(
+       nullif(current_setting('request.jwt.claims', true), '')::jsonb ->> 'sub',
+       nullif(current_setting('request.jwt.claim.sub', true), '')
+     ), '')::uuid $$;
+
+CREATE TABLE public.profiles (id uuid PRIMARY KEY, user_id uuid NOT NULL);
+CREATE TABLE public.contacts (id uuid PRIMARY KEY, user_id uuid NOT NULL);
+CREATE TABLE public.conversation_snoozes (id uuid PRIMARY KEY, snoozed_by uuid NOT NULL, contact_id uuid, snoozed_until timestamptz);
+CREATE TABLE public.favorite_contacts (id uuid PRIMARY KEY, user_id uuid NOT NULL, contact_id uuid NOT NULL);
+CREATE TABLE public.pinned_conversations (id uuid PRIMARY KEY, pinned_by uuid NOT NULL, contact_id uuid NOT NULL);
+
+ALTER TABLE public.conversation_snoozes ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
+ALTER TABLE public.favorite_contacts ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
+ALTER TABLE public.pinned_conversations ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
+
+GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON public.conversation_snoozes TO authenticated, anon;
+GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON public.favorite_contacts TO authenticated, anon;
+GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON public.pinned_conversations TO authenticated, anon;
+GRANT ALL ON public.profiles TO authenticated, anon;
+GRANT ALL ON public.contacts TO authenticated, anon;
+SQL
+
+# Policies de apoio (SELECT/DELETE de snoozes + "manage" originais): bytes saidos
+# do proprio arquivo da 20260409, sem reescrever. As "manage" sao derrubadas
+# pela 20260924230500 (DROP IF EXISTS), como em producao.
+grep -E '^CREATE POLICY "Users can (view|create|delete) own snoozes" ON|^CREATE POLICY "Users can manage own (pins|favorites)" ON' \

+[[ "$(wc -l < "$tmp_dir/apoio.sql")" == "5" ]] || fail "extracao das policies de apoio: esperado 5, obtido $(wc -l < "$tmp_dir/apoio.sql")"
+
+psql_file "$tmp_dir/pre.sql"
+psql_file "$tmp_dir/apoio.sql"
+psql_file "$origin_idor"
+
+# Massa da prova, como superusuario (bypassa RLS): perfil/contato/linhas da dona.
+UID_ALICE='11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111'
+ALICE='{"sub":"11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111","role":"authenticated"}'
+P1='00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001'
+C1='11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111'
+psql_sql "INSERT INTO public.profiles (id,user_id) VALUES ('$P1','$UID_ALICE')" >/dev/null

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# PE-09 (paridade V3 -> V2, docs 10..40, t_59d66c7a):
+# "A caixa promete buscar e-mails, remetentes, assuntos, anexos, mas a busca local
+#  so alcanca email_threads (subject/snippet/last_from_*); corpo (email_messages.body_text)
+#  e nome do anexo (email_attachments.filename) ficam de fora."
+#
+# Roda em Postgres descartavel com os papeis REAIS (anon/authenticated/service_role) e as
+# definicoes REAIS de gmail_accounts/email_threads/email_messages/email_attachments e das
+# policies (20260403105341 e 20260827210200):
+#   BLOCO A ‚Äî defeito: a busca por email_threads nao acha palavra do corpo nem nome de anexo.
+#   BLOCO B ‚Äî migration real aplicada (psql -f): acha corpo e anexo, diz onde casou, respeita
+#             a RLS (nao vaza para outro dono nem para quem nao tem conta), nao devolve a
+#             caixa inteira em termo vazio/curinga, pagina por p_after, e o plano usa o
+#             indice de trigrama.
+#   BLOCO C ‚Äî a linha "-- Rollback:" do proprio arquivo roda e remove a funcao e os indices.
+
+set -Eeuo pipefail
+
+repo_root="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
+migration="$repo_root/supabase/migrations/20261013230000_search_email_threads.sql"
+postgres_image="${SEARCH_EMAIL_TEST_POSTGRES_IMAGE:-postgres:17-alpine}"
+container_name="zapp-v2-search-email-test-$$"
+passed=0
+
+cleanup() {
+  if [[ "$container_name" =~ ^zapp-v2-search-email-test-[0-9]+$ ]]; then
+    docker rm -f "$container_name" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+  fi
+}
+trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM
+
+fail() { printf '[FAIL] %s\n' "$1" >&2; exit 1; }
+pass() { printf '[PASS] %s\n' "$1"; ((passed += 1)); }
+
+psql_sql() {
+  docker exec "$container_name" psql -X -qAt -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -U postgres -d postgres -c "$1"
+}
+psql_file() {
+  docker exec -i "$container_name" psql -X -qAt -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -U postgres -d postgres < "$1"
+}
+as_role() {
+  local role="$1" jwt="$2" sql="$3"
+  docker exec "$container_name" psql -X -qAt -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -U postgres -d postgres \
+    -c "SET ROLE $role; SELECT set_config('request.jwt.claims', '$jwt', false); $sql"
+}
+expect_value() {
+  local l="$1" e="$2" s="$3" a
+  a="$(psql_sql "$s" | tail -n1)"
+  [[ "$a" == "$e" ]] || fail "$l: esperado '$e', obtido '$a'"
+  pass "$l"
+}
+expect_value_role() {
+  local l="$1" e="$2" r="$3" j="$4" s="$5" a
+  a="$(as_role "$r" "$j" "$s" | tail -n1)"
+  [[ "$a" == "$e" ]] || fail "$l: esperado '$e', obtido '$a'"
+  pass "$l"
+}
+expect_ok_role() {
+  local l="$1" r="$2" j="$3" s="$4"
+  as_role "$r" "$j" "$s" >/dev/null || fail "$l: deveria ter sucesso (como $r)"
+  pass "$l"
+}
+expect_error_role() {
+  local l="$1" needle="$2" r="$3" j="$4" s="$5" out st
+  set +e; out="$(as_role "$r" "$j" "$s" 2>&1)"; st=$?; set -e
+  (( st == 0 )) && { printf '%s\n' "$out" >&2; fail "$l: deveria falhar, mas passou"; }
+  [[ "$out" == *"$needle"* ]] || { printf '%s\n' "$out" >&2; fail "$l: esperava '$needle' no erro"; }
+  pass "$l"
+}
+
+command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail 'Docker nao esta instalado'
+docker info >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail 'Docker daemon nao esta acessivel'
+[[ -f "$migration" ]] || fail "migration nao encontrada: $migration"
+
+printf '== container: %s (imagem %s) ==\n' "$container_name" "$postgres_image"
+docker run --rm -d --name "$container_name" -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=test_only "$postgres_image" >/dev/null
+
+ready=0
+for _ in $(seq 1 90); do
+  if psql_sql 'SELECT 1' >/dev/null 2>&1; then ready=$((ready + 1)); (( ready >= 2 )) && break; else ready=0; fi
+  sleep 1
+done

+
+# --- paginacao por p_after ---
+expect_value_role 'B.16 p_limit=1 traz so a mais recente (T1)' '1' 'authenticated' "$U1" \

+P_AFTER="$(as_role 'authenticated' "$U1" "SELECT last_message_at FROM public.search_email_threads('$A1','cliente',1,NULL::timestamptz);" | tail -n1)"

+  "SELECT count(*) FROM public.search_email_threads('$A1','%',20,NULL::timestamptz);"
+expect_value_role 'B.21 curinga _ e literal e nao quebra (sem regex do usuario)' '0' 'authenticated' "$U1" \
+  "SELECT count(*) FROM public.search_email_threads('$A1','_',20,NULL::timestamptz);"
+expect_value_role 'B.22 termo so de curingas escapado nao estoura erro' '0' 'authenticated' "$U1" \
+  "SELECT count(*) FROM public.search_email_threads('$A1','\%_',20,NULL::timestamptz);"
+
+# --- service_role (BYPASSRLS) ---
+expect_value_role 'B.23 service_role acha a thread da A2' '1' 'service_role' "$SVC" \
+  "SELECT count(*) FROM public.search_email_threads('$A2','orcamento',20,NULL::timestamptz);"
+
+# --- anon negado, papel real ---
+expect_error_role 'B.24 anon nao executa a RPC (permission denied)' \
+  'permission denied' 'anon' "$ANON" \
+  "SELECT count(*) FROM public.search_email_threads('$A1','orcamento',20,NULL::timestamptz);"
+
+# --- plano usa o indice de trigrama ---
+PLANO="$(docker exec "$container_name" psql -X -qAt -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -U postgres -d postgres -c \
+  "SET enable_seqscan=off; EXPLAIN SELECT id FROM public.email_messages WHERE body_text ILIKE '%orcamento%';")"
+[[ "$PLANO" == *"email_messages_body_text_trgm_idx"* ]] || { printf '%s\n' "$PLANO" >&2; fail 'B.25 o plano nao usa o indice de trigrama'; }
+pass 'B.25 o plano de busca do corpo usa email_messages_body_text_trgm_idx'
+PLANO_ATT="$(docker exec "$container_name" psql -X -qAt -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -U postgres -d postgres -c \
+  "SET enable_seqscan=off; EXPLAIN SELECT id FROM public.email_attachments WHERE filename ILIKE '%cliente%';")"
+[[ "$PLANO_ATT" == *"email_attachments_filename_trgm_idx"* ]] || { printf '%s\n' "$PLANO_ATT" >&2; fail 'B.26 o plano do anexo nao usa o indice de trigrama'; }
+pass 'B.26 o plano de busca do anexo usa email_attachments_filename_trgm_idx'
+
+printf '\n============ BLOCO C ‚Äî rollback do proprio arquivo ============\n'
+sed -n '1,12p' "$migration" | sed -n 's/^--   //p' > "$tmp_dir/rollback.sql"
+[[ -s "$tmp_dir/rollback.sql" ]] || fail 'a migration nao tem as linhas de rollback executavel'
+psql_file "$tmp_dir/rollback.sql" >/dev/null
+pass 'C.1 as linhas de rollback executaram sem erro'
+expect_value 'C.2 a funcao sumiu' '0' \
+  "SELECT count(*) FROM pg_proc WHERE proname='search_email_threads';"
+expect_value 'C.3 os indices sumiram' '0' \
+  "SELECT count(*) FROM pg_indexes WHERE schemaname='public' AND indexname IN ('email_messages_body_text_trgm_idx','email_attachments_filename_trgm_idx');"
+
+psql_file "$migration" >/dev/null
+expect_value 'C.4 reaplicar a migration e idempotente (funcao de volta)' '1' \
+  "SELECT count(*) FROM pg_proc WHERE proname='search_email_threads';"

+printf '\nPE-09 search_email_threads (%s): %s cenarios aprovados.\n' "$postgres_image" "$passed"

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# n-148 (P3 ¬∑ SEC-RLS_TAREFAS_EMAIL_LIGACOES-07) ‚Äî search_path com pg_temp nas duas funcoes
+# SECURITY DEFINER que o audit adversarial encontrou com `SET search_path = public`:
+# public.is_admin_or_supervisor(uuid) e public.get_own_gmail_accounts().
+#
+# O estado ANTERIOR vem dos ARQUIVOS REAIS do repo, aplicados nesta ordem:
+#   supabase/migrations/20251215025014_fcc5bc79-55e3-4972-8765-6a7840fdce5a.sql (cria is_admin_or_supervisor)
+#   supabase/migrations/20260828210000_get_own_gmail_accounts_filter_active.sql (cria get_own_gmail_accounts)
+# O pre.sql deste teste contem SO stubs dos pre-requisitos que esses arquivos exigem
+# (papeis anon/authenticated/service_role, auth.uid()/auth.role(), auth.users, storage.*,
+# contacts/profiles/whatsapp_connections, publication supabase_realtime, tabela gmail_accounts)
+# e NAO reescreve corpo, assinatura nem ACL das funcoes.
+#
+# DISCRIMINADOR vermelho->verde: SO proconfig (A1/A2 x B1/B2). Os corpos das duas funcoes
+# qualificam public.* (public.user_roles, public.gmail_accounts), por isso temp tables
+# hostis NAO shadowam o resultado nem sem a correcao: A6/B6 passam antes e depois e sao
+# guardas de regressao, nao prova do defeito.
+#
+# Roda o MESMO roteiro num PostgreSQL 17 DESCARTAVEL e aplica o ARQUIVO de migration REAL:
+#   BLOCO A ‚Äî estado ANTERIOR (arquivos reais, search_path = public, sem pg_temp):
+#             registra o defeito (proconfig sem pg_temp, A1/A2) e prova o contrato
+#             funcional das duas funcoes rodando como o papel authenticated com
+#             request.jwt.claims. A0a/A0b mostram o ACL ainda ABERTO (default PUBLIC).
+#   BLOCO B ‚Äî migration aplicada: search_path passa a `public, pg_temp`; o contrato
+#             funcional nao muda, o ACL fecha (B7-B10, fechado PELA migration, que e a
+#             unica a tocar em REVOKE/GRANT neste teste) e as temp tables HOSTIS seguem
+#             sem shadowar (B6, guarda de regressao).
+#
+# Sem dependencia de banco/stack do cartao: sobe container proprio (roles anon/
+# authenticated/service_role sao globais ao cluster ‚Äî por isso SKIP_DOCKER_SHIM=1).
+
+set -Eeuo pipefail
+
+repo_root="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
+migration="$repo_root/supabase/migrations/20261010150628_search_path_pg_temp_is_admin_get_own_gmail.sql"
+origin_is_admin="$repo_root/supabase/migrations/20251215025014_fcc5bc79-55e3-4972-8765-6a7840fdce5a.sql"
+origin_gmail="$repo_root/supabase/migrations/20260828210000_get_own_gmail_accounts_filter_active.sql"
+postgres_image="${SEARCH_PATH_PG_TEMP_TEST_POSTGRES_IMAGE:-postgres:17-alpine}"
+container_name="zapp-v2-search-path-pg-temp-test-$$"
+
+cleanup() {
+  if [[ "$container_name" =~ ^zapp-v2-search-path-pg-temp-test-[0-9]+$ ]]; then
+    docker rm -f "$container_name" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+  fi
+}
+trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM
+
+fail() { printf '[FAIL] %s\n' "$1" >&2; exit 1; }
+
+psql_sql() {
+  docker exec "$container_name" psql -X -qAt -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -U postgres -d postgres -c "$1"
+}
+psql_file() {
+  docker exec -i "$container_name" psql -X -qAt -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -U postgres -d postgres < "$1"
+}
+expect_value() {
+  local label="$1" expected="$2" sql="$3" actual
+  actual="$(psql_sql "$sql" | tail -n1)"
+  [[ "$actual" == "$expected" ]] || fail "$label: esperado '$expected', obtido '$actual'"
+  printf '[PASS] %s\n' "$label"
+}
+
+command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail 'Docker nao esta instalado'
+docker info >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail 'Docker daemon nao esta acessivel'
+[[ -f "$migration" ]] || fail "migration nao encontrada: $migration"
+[[ -f "$origin_is_admin" ]] || fail "origem real nao encontrada: $origin_is_admin"
+[[ -f "$origin_gmail" ]] || fail "origem real nao encontrada: $origin_gmail"
+
+docker run --rm -d --name "$container_name" -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=test_only "$postgres_image" >/dev/null

+ready_checks=0
+for _ in $(seq 1 90); do
+  if psql_sql 'SELECT 1' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    ready_checks=$((ready_checks + 1)); (( ready_checks >= 2 )) && break
+  else ready_checks=0; fi
+  sleep 1
+done
+(( ready_checks >= 2 )) || fail 'PostgreSQL descartavel nao ficou pronto de forma estavel'
+
+tmp_dir="$(mktemp -d)"

+CREATE ROLE anon NOLOGIN;
+CREATE ROLE authenticated NOLOGIN;
+CREATE ROLE service_role NOLOGIN BYPASSRLS;

+CREATE SCHEMA auth;
+CREATE FUNCTION auth.uid() RETURNS uuid LANGUAGE sql STABLE
+  AS $$ SELECT nullif(coalesce(
+       nullif(current_setting('request.jwt.claims', true), '')::jsonb ->> 'sub',
+       nullif(current_setting('request.jwt.claim.sub', true), '')
+     ), '')::uuid $$;
+CREATE FUNCTION auth.role() RETURNS text LANGUAGE sql STABLE
+  AS $$ SELECT coalesce(
+       nullif(current_setting('request.jwt.claim.role', true), ''),
+       nullif(current_setting('request.jwt.claims', true), '')::jsonb ->> 'role'
+     )::text $$;

+-- auth.users: a origem 20251215025014 referencia auth.users(id) em FKs e num trigger.
+CREATE TABLE auth.users (id uuid PRIMARY KEY);
+
+-- storage: a origem 20251215025014 insere em storage.buckets e cria policies em storage.objects.
+CREATE SCHEMA storage;
+CREATE TABLE storage.buckets (id text PRIMARY KEY, name text, public boolean);
+CREATE TABLE storage.objects (id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), bucket_id text);
+
+-- Tabelas referenciadas por FKs da origem 20251215025014 (tabela calls).
+CREATE TABLE public.contacts (id uuid PRIMARY KEY);

+CREATE TABLE public.whatsapp_connections (id uuid PRIMARY KEY);
+
+-- A origem 20251215025014 termina com ALTER PUBLICATION supabase_realtime ADD TABLE.
+CREATE PUBLICATION supabase_realtime;
+
+-- gmail_accounts: stub fiel (so as colunas que get_own_gmail_accounts le).
+-- A FUNCAO vem do arquivo real 20260828210000, aplicado abaixo.
+CREATE TABLE public.gmail_accounts (
+  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
+  user_id uuid NOT NULL,
+  email_address text NOT NULL,
+  is_active boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
+  sync_status text,
+  last_sync_at timestamptz,
+  last_error text,
+  token_expires_at timestamptz,

+  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
+);
+ALTER TABLE public.gmail_accounts ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
+SQL

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# R2-API-058 / #230 (P2, area banco): "Alerta mensal de custo repete e-mail em cada
+# execucao diaria do cron".
+#
+# O job do cron `searchbox-budget-alert` (migration REAL 20261002601230) rodava, todo dia,
+# DUAS instrucoes: SELECT public.notify_searchbox_budget()  (canal app, com ledger mensal em
+# notifications) e SELECT net.http_post(...searchbox-budget-alert...) INCONDICIONAL. A edge so
+# consulta o consumo e envia: enquanto o mes ficasse acima do limiar, o e-mail repetia em CADA
+# execucao diaria -- um alerta por dia em vez de um por mes.
+#
+# Este contrato roda o MESMO roteiro no mesmo container, em dois blocos:
+#   BLOCO A -- estado ANTERIOR (defeito): aplica a migration real 20261002601230 e executa o
+#              comando REAL do cron.job duas vezes no mesmo mes. O canal app deduplica (1
+#              notificacao), mas saem DOIS net.http_post -> o defeito, medido no POST que o
+#              cron faria de verdade.
+#   BLOCO B -- migration nova aplicada (20261006235031): o mes e reivindicado de forma atomica
+#              no ledger proprio do canal de e-mail (public.searchbox_budget_alert_emails, PK=mes)
+#              ANTES do envio; so o mes novo (ou um mes com falha CONFIRMADA) faz o POST. Dois
+#              ticks do mesmo mes = UM POST. status 'sent'/'pending'/'uncertain' nao reenviam.
+#   BLOCO C -- rollback: as linhas `-- Rollback:` da migration sao extraidas e EXECUTADAS; o
+#              job volta ao comando anterior (guardado como dado pela propria migration), o
+#              ledger, a tabela de estado e a funcao nova somem -- e o defeito volta a acontecer
+#              (2 POSTs), provando que o rollback desfaz o que a migration fez.
+#
+# Nao ha host literal em nenhum lugar deste contrato: a URL do canal e CAPTURADA do comando
+# vigente do job, exatamente como a migration nova faz (a trava do modo V2 proibe o host no SQL).
+#
+# LIMITE DECLARADO: o container nao tem o Vault nem o pg_cron do Supabase. O pre.sql cria STUBS
+# fieis: cron.job + cron.schedule/unschedule (com o UPSERT por (jobname, username) do pg_cron 1.6),
+# Vault (vault.decrypted_secrets) e net.http_post trocado por uma TABELA DE CAPTURA -- o teste
+# mede os POSTs que o cron dispararia, sem rede. As funcoes e o SQL sob prova vem dos ARQUIVOS de
+# supabase/migrations/ (nada de policy/ledger recriado a mao no teste).
+#
+# Uso: bash scripts/db-audit/searchbox-budget-alert-monthly-idempotency.test.sh
+#      SEARCHBOX_ALERT_TEST_POSTGRES_IMAGE=postgres:17-alpine (default)
+
+set -Eeuo pipefail
+
+repo_root="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
+if [[ -n "${MIGRATIONS_DIR:-}" ]]; then
+  migrations_dir="$MIGRATIONS_DIR"
+elif [[ -d "$repo_root/supabase/migrations" ]]; then
+  migrations_dir="$repo_root/supabase/migrations"
+else
+  migrations_dir="${ZAPP_REPO_ROOT:-$HOME/projetos/Zapp_Web_V2}/supabase/migrations"
+fi
+migration_antiga="$migrations_dir/20261002601230_searchbox_budget_alert_cron.sql"
+migration_nova="$migrations_dir/20261006235031_searchbox_budget_alert_email_ledger.sql"
+postgres_image="${SEARCHBOX_ALERT_TEST_POSTGRES_IMAGE:-postgres:17-alpine}"
+container_name="zapp-v2-searchbox-alert-test-$$"
+
+cleanup() {
+  if [[ "$container_name" =~ ^zapp-v2-searchbox-alert-test-[0-9]+$ ]]; then
+    docker rm -f "$container_name" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+  fi
+}
+trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM
+
+fail() { printf '[FAIL] %s\n' "$1" >&2; exit 1; }
+pass() { printf '[PASS] %s\n' "$1"; }
+
+psql_sql() {
+  docker exec "$container_name" psql -X -qAt -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -U postgres -d postgres -c "$1"
+}
+psql_file() {
+  docker exec -i "$container_name" psql -X -qAt -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -U postgres -d postgres < "$1"
+}
+# Roda como o PAPEL REAL (nunca como postgres): e o unico jeito de provar ACL/RLS.
+as_role() {
+  local papel="$1" sql="$2"
+  docker exec "$container_name" psql -X -qAt -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -U postgres -d postgres \
+    -c "SET ROLE $papel; $sql"
+}
+expect_value() {
+  local label="$1" expected="$2" sql="$3" actual
+  actual="$(psql_sql "$sql" | tail -n1)"
+  [[ "$actual" == "$expected" ]] || fail "$label: esperado '$expected', obtido '$actual'"
+  pass "$label"
+}
+expect_error_as() {
+  local label="$1" needle="$2" papel="$3" sql="$4" out st
+  set +e; out="$(as_role "$papel" "$sql" 2>&1)"; st=$?; set -e
+  (( st == 0 )) && { printf '%s\n' "$out" >&2; fail "$label: deveria falhar, mas passou"; }
+  [[ "$out" == *"$needle"* ]] || { printf '%s\n' "$out" >&2; fail "$label: esperava '$needle'"; }
+  pass "$label"
+}
+expect_value_as() {
+  local label="$1" expected="$2" papel="$3" sql="$4" actual
+  actual="$(as_role "$papel" "$sql" | tail -n1)"
+  [[ "$actual" == "$expected" ]] || fail "$label: esperado '$expected', obtido '$actual'"
+  pass "$label"
+}
+
+# Executa o comando REAL do cron.job -- nao uma reimplementacao do que o job faz.
+tick() {
+  local cmd
+  cmd="$(psql_sql "SELECT command FROM cron.job WHERE jobname = 'searchbox-budget-alert'")"
+  [[ -n "$cmd" ]] || fail 'job searchbox-budget-alert nao existe'
+  docker exec "$container_name" psql -X -qAt -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -U postgres -d postgres -c "$cmd" >/dev/null
+}
+SQL_CAPTURAS='SELECT count(*) FROM net.http_capture'
+SQL_NOTIF="SELECT count(*) FROM public.notifications WHERE type = 'searchbox_budget_alert'"
+reset_medicao() { psql_sql 'TRUNCATE net.http_capture'; psql_sql 'DELETE FROM public.notifications'; }
+MES="to_char((now() at time zone 'America/Sao_Paulo'), 'YYYY-MM')"
+LEDGER='public.searchbox_budget_alert_emails'
+
+command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail 'Docker nao esta instalado'
+docker info >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail 'Docker daemon nao esta acessivel'
+[[ -f "$migration_antiga" ]] || fail "migration nao encontrada: $migration_antiga"
+[[ -f "$migration_nova" ]] || fail "migration nao encontrada: $migration_nova"
+
+printf '== container: %s (imagem %s)\n' "$container_name" "$postgres_image"
+docker run --rm -d --name "$container_name" -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=test_only "$postgres_image" >/dev/null
+
+ready=0
+for _ in $(seq 1 90); do
+  if psql_sql 'SELECT 1' >/dev/null 2>&1; then ready=$((ready + 1)); (( ready >= 2 )) && break; else ready=0; fi
+  sleep 1
+done
+(( ready >= 2 )) || fail 'PostgreSQL descartavel nao ficou pronto de forma estavel'

+mkdir -p "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}"
+tmp_dir="$(mktemp -d)"
+trap 'rm -rf "$tmp_dir"; cleanup' EXIT INT TERM

+cat > "$tmp_dir/pre.sql" <<'SQL'
+-- ‚îÄ‚îÄ roles do PostgREST (idempotente) ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ
+DO $$
+BEGIN
+  IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = 'anon') THEN CREATE ROLE anon NOLOGIN; END IF;
+  IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = 'authenticated') THEN CREATE ROLE authenticated NOLOGIN; END IF;
+  IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = 'service_role') THEN CREATE ROLE service_role NOLOGIN BYPASSRLS; END IF;
+END $$;
+
+-- ‚îÄ‚îÄ tabelas minimas que as funcoes REAIS tocam ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ
+CREATE TABLE public.profiles (

+);

+-- ‚îÄ‚îÄ Vault (stub): a subquery do segredo de cron do job ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ
+CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS vault;
+CREATE TABLE vault.secrets (
+  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
+  name text UNIQUE,
+  description text,
+  secret text,
+  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
+);
+CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW vault.decrypted_secrets AS
+  SELECT id, name, description, secret AS decrypted_secret, created_at FROM vault.secrets;
+
+-- ‚îÄ‚îÄ net.http_post trocado por TABELA DE CAPTURA: mede os POSTs, sem rede ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ‚îÄ
+CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS net;
+CREATE TABLE net.http_capture (
+  id bigserial PRIMARY KEY,
+  url text,
+  body jsonb,
+  headers jsonb,
+  timeout_milliseconds integer,
+  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT statement_timestamp()
+);
+CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION net.http_post(
+  url text,
+  body jsonb DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
+  headers jsonb DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
+  timeout_milliseconds integer DEFAULT 5000
+) RETURNS bigint LANGUAGE sql VOLATILE AS $$
+  INSERT INTO net.http_capture (url, body, headers, timeout_milliseconds)
+  VALUES (url, body, headers, timeout_milliseconds)
+  RETURNING id
+$$;
+
+-- ‚îÄ‚îÄ pg_cron (stub FIEL ao 1.6): schedule FAZ UPSERT por (jobname, username) ‚îÄ‚îÄ
+-- E exatamente o comportamento em que a migration nova se apoia (job de mesmo nome e
+-- ATUALIZADO, nao duplicado) -- se o stub nao upsertasse, o teste mentiria.
+CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS cron;
+CREATE TABLE cron.job (
+  jobid bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
+  jobname text,
+  schedule text,
+  command text,
+  active boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
+  username text NOT NULL DEFAULT current_user,
+  CONSTRAINT cron_job_jobname_username_key UNIQUE (jobname, username)
+);
+CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION cron.schedule(p_name text, p_schedule text, p_command text)
+RETURNS bigint LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
+DECLARE v bigint;
+BEGIN
+  SELECT jobid INTO v FROM cron.job WHERE jobname = p_name AND username = current_user;
+  IF v IS NULL THEN
+    INSERT INTO cron.job (jobname, schedule, command, username)
+    VALUES (p_name, p_schedule, p_command, current_user)
+    RETURNING jobid INTO v;
+  ELSE
+    UPDATE cron.job SET schedule = p_schedule, command = p_command WHERE jobid = v;
+  END IF;
+  RETURN v;
+END $$;
+CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION cron.unschedule(p_name text)
+RETURNS boolean LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
+DECLARE v boolean;
+BEGIN
+  DELETE FROM cron.job WHERE jobname = p_name AND username = current_user RETURNING true INTO v;
+  RETURN COALESCE(v, false);
+END $$;
+SQL

+#!/usr/bin/env bash

+# (docs/audits/SEGURANCA_RLS_TAREFAS_EMAIL_LIGACOES_2026-10-07.md)
+#
+# O INSERT de `deal_activities`, `calls` e `conversation_tasks` validava s√≥ o AUTOR
+# (`performed_by` / `agent_id` / `created_by`), nunca o ALVO (`deal_id` / `contact_id`).
+# Qualquer usu√°rio autenticado gravava item de hist√≥rico apontando para neg√≥cio/contato fora
+# do seu escopo, e n√£o existe policy de UPDATE/DELETE nessas tabelas para o cliente corrigir.
+#
+# BLOCO A (antes): com as policies correntes (o defeito, texto extra√≠do dos arquivos atuais ‚Äî
+#   ver `prestate.sql` abaixo) o agente B grava atividade no neg√≥cio do agente A, chama e cria
+#   tarefa no contato do agente A ‚Äî e consegue. O mesmo arquivo fixa o controle leg√≠timo.
+# BLOCO B (depois): com a corre√ß√£o (20261009090603_sec_y25_01_insert_alvo.sql) os tr√™s ataques
+#   falham, os fluxos leg√≠timos seguem passando, `anon` √© negado pelo RLS (tem GRANT, como em
+#   produ√ß√£o) e `service_role` (BYPASSRLS) segue liberado.
+# BLOCO C: o rollback DOCUMENTADO no cabe√ßalho da migration √© extra√≠do do pr√≥prio arquivo e
+#   executado ‚Äî o ataque volta a passar (prova que √© a policy da corre√ß√£o que barra) ‚Äî e a
+#   corre√ß√£o √© reaplicada (idempotente).
+#

+#   teste pega a guarda removida.
+#
+# Roda o SQL de verdade em PostgreSQL descart√°vel, aplicando as migrations REAIS e executando

+fail() { printf '[FAIL] %s\n' "$1" >&2; exit 1; }

+# psql_como <role> <sub|-> <sql>: roda <sql> como o papel real, com o JWT do usu√°rio.
+psql_como() {
+  local role="$1" sub="$2" sql="$3"
+  if [[ "$sub" == "-" ]]; then
+    psql_sql "SET ROLE $role; $sql"
+  else
+    psql_sql "SET ROLE $role; SELECT set_config('request.jwt.claim.sub','$sub',false); $sql"
+  fi
+}

+expect_ok() {
+  local label="$1" role="$2" sub="$3" sql="$4" out status
+  set +e
+  out="$(psql_como "$role" "$sub" "$sql" 2>&1)"
+  status=$?
+  set -e
+  if (( status != 0 )); then
+    printf '%s\n' "$out" >&2
+    fail "$label deveria passar (exit $status)"
+  fi
+  [[ "$(printf '%s' "$out" | tail -n1)" == "1" ]] || fail "$label deveria inserir 1 linha, obtido '$out'"
+  printf '[PASS] %s\n' "$label"
+}

+expect_failure() {
+  local label="$1" role="$2" sub="$3" sql="$4" out status
+  set +e
+  out="$(psql_como "$role" "$sub" "$sql" 2>&1)"

+  set -e
+  if (( status == 0 )); then
+    printf '%s\n' "$out" >&2
+    fail "$label deveria falhar"
+  fi
+  if [[ "${SEC_Y25_DEBUG:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
+    printf '      negado com: %s\n' "$(printf '%s' "$out" | grep -m1 -E '^ERROR:' || printf '(sem ERROR na saida)')"
+  fi
+  printf '[PASS] %s\n' "$label"
+}

+UPD_STATUS="WITH upd AS (UPDATE public.calls SET status = 'answered', answered_at = now() WHERE id = CALL_ID RETURNING 1) SELECT count(*) FROM upd"
+ups() { printf '%s' "$UPSERT_CALL" | sed "s/CALL_ID/$1/; s/CONTATO/$2/; s/PERFIL/$3/"; }
+upc() { printf '%s' "$UPD_CALL" | sed "s/CALL_ID/$1/; s/CONTATO/$2/"; }

+/**
+ * R2-SLA-003: prova, num PostgreSQL 17 descartavel, que
+ * register_first_response_internal classifica first_response_breached contra o

+ *   contact > company > job_title > contact_type > queue > agent,

+ * Antes da migration de prazo granular o caso "regra de 2 min + resposta aos

+ * este teste fica VERMELHO. Depois, VERDE.

+ * ULTIMA versao de cada nome, em ordem de versao) ‚Äî nada de copiar SQL para o
+ * teste nem de so conferir texto.

+function docker(args, input) {
+  return execFileSync('docker', args, {
+    input,
+    encoding: 'utf8',
+    stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
+  });
+}
+
+function sleepMs(ms) {
+  Atomics.wait(new Int32Array(new SharedArrayBuffer(4)), 0, 0, ms);
+}
+
+function psql(sql) {
+  return docker(
+    ['exec', '-i', CONTAINER, 'psql', '-X', '-At', '-v', 'ON_ERROR_STOP=1',
+      '-U', 'postgres', '-d', 'postgres'],
+    sql,
+  );
+}
+
+function waitForPostgres() {
+  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 60; attempt += 1) {
+    let logs = '';
+    try {
+      logs = docker(['logs', CONTAINER]);
+    } catch {
+      logs = '';
+    }
+    if (logs.includes('PostgreSQL init process complete; ready for start up.')) {
+      try {
+        docker(['exec', CONTAINER, 'psql', '-X', '-At', '-v', 'ON_ERROR_STOP=1',
+          '-U', 'postgres', '-d', 'postgres', '-c', 'SELECT 1']);
+        return;
+      } catch {
+        // servidor final ainda nao aceita conexao; tenta de novo
+      }
+    }
+    sleepMs(1000);
+  }
+  throw new Error('PostgreSQL de teste nao ficou pronto em 60 segundos.');
+}
+
+/**
+ * Captura o bloco `CREATE [OR REPLACE] FUNCTION public.<nome>(...) $<tag>$...
+ * $<tag>$;` MAIS RECENTE do arquivo. O primeiro dollar-quote apos o cabecalho e
+ * o corpo da funcao (o cabecalho nao contem dollar-quote).
+ */
+function findCreateFunctionBlock(sql, name) {
+  const header = new RegExp(
+    `create\\s+(?:or\\s+replace\\s+)?function\\s+public\\.${name}\\s*\\(`,
+    'gi',
+  );
+  let start = -1;
+  for (const match of sql.matchAll(header)) start = match.index;
+  if (start === -1) return null;
+
+  const tagMatch = sql.slice(start).match(/\$[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\$|\$\$/);
+  if (!tagMatch) return null;
+  const tag = tagMatch[0];
+  const bodyStart = start + tagMatch.index + tag.length;
+  const close = sql.indexOf(tag, bodyStart);
+  if (close === -1) return null;
+  const tail = sql.slice(close + tag.length).match(/^\s*;/);
+  if (!tail) return null;
+  return sql.slice(start, close + tag.length + tail[0].length);
+}
+
+/**
+ * Percorre as migrations em ordem de versao e devolve a ultima definicao de
+ * cada nome pedido (como o banco fica depois de aplicar a cadeia inteira).
+ */
+function lastFunctionDefs(names) {
+  const files = fs.readdirSync(MIGRATIONS_DIR)
+    .filter((file) => /^\d{14}_.*\.sql$/.test(file))
+    .sort();
+  const last = new Map();
+  for (const file of files) {
+    const sql = fs.readFileSync(path.join(MIGRATIONS_DIR, file), 'utf8');
+    for (const name of names) {
+      const block = findCreateFunctionBlock(sql, name);
+      if (block) last.set(name, { file, sql: block });
+    }
+  }
+  return last;
+}
+
+function lastDefiningFile(name) {
+  const files = fs.readdirSync(MIGRATIONS_DIR)
+    .filter((file) => /^\d{14}_.*\.sql$/.test(file))
+    .sort();
+  const needle = new RegExp(
+    `create\\s+(?:or\\s+replace\\s+)?function\\s+public\\.${name}\\s*\\(`,
+    'i',
+  );
+  let found = null;
+  for (const file of files) {
+    if (needle.test(fs.readFileSync(path.join(MIGRATIONS_DIR, file), 'utf8'))) {
+      found = file;
+    }
+  }
+  return found;
+}

+/**
+ * Roda um cenario inteiro numa UNICA transacao (BEGIN...ROLLBACK): os SELECTs
+ * rotulados imprimem "rotulo|valor" e nada sobra no banco.
+ */
+function runScenario(sql) {
+  const out = psql(`BEGIN;\n${sql}\nROLLBACK;\n`);
+  const rows = new Map();
+  for (const line of out.split('\n')) {
+    const idx = line.indexOf('|');
+    if (idx > 0) rows.set(line.slice(0, idx), line.slice(idx + 1));
+  }
+  return rows;
+}
+
+function registerCall(contactId, respondedAtExpr) {
+  return `SELECT public.${REGISTER_FN}('${contactId}', ${respondedAtExpr}, ${respondedAtExpr});`;
+}
+
+function breachProbe(label, contactId) {
+  return `SELECT '${label}', first_response_breached FROM public.conversation_sla WHERE contact_id = '${contactId}';`;
+}
+
+function resolverProbe(label, contactId) {
+  return `SELECT '${label}', public.${RESOLVER_FN}('${contactId}');`;
+}

+test('regra ATIVA de 2 min (nivel contact) classifica resposta aos 3 min como breach', () => {
+  const contact = '11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111';
+  const rows = runScenario(`
+INSERT INTO public.contacts (id) VALUES ('${contact}');
+INSERT INTO public.sla_rules (name, first_response_minutes, contact_id, priority)
+  VALUES ('vip-2min', 2, '${contact}', 10);
+INSERT INTO public.messages (contact_id, sender, status, created_at) VALUES
+  ('${contact}', 'contact', 'delivered', '${T}'::timestamptz),
+  ('${contact}', 'agent', 'sent', '${T}'::timestamptz + interval '3 minutes');
+${registerCall(contact, `'${T}'::timestamptz + interval '3 minutes'`)}
+${breachProbe('caso_2min_3min', contact)}
+  `);
+  assert.equal(rows.get('caso_2min_3min'), 't',
+    'regra de 2 min + resposta aos 3 min deveria marcar first_response_breached=true');
+});

+test('sem regra nem configuracao: padrao do sistema (5 min) segue valendo', () => {

+  const c6min = '33333333-3333-3333-3333-333333333333';
+  const rows = runScenario(`

+INSERT INTO public.messages (contact_id, sender, status, created_at) VALUES
+  ('${c3min}', 'contact', 'delivered', '${T}'::timestamptz),

+import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
+import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
+import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';
+
+const __dirname = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
+const BASELINE_PATH = join(__dirname, 'storage-buckets-baseline.json');
+
+export function loadBaseline() {
+  const raw = readFileSync(BASELINE_PATH, 'utf-8');
+  return JSON.parse(raw);
+}
+
+export function validateStorageBuckets(currentBuckets, baseline) {
+  const failures = [];
+  const baselineById = new Map(baseline.buckets.map((b) => [b.id, b]));
+  const currentById = new Map(currentBuckets.map((b) => [b.id, b]));
+
+  for (const bucket of currentBuckets) {
+    const expected = baselineById.get(bucket.id);
+    if (!expected) {
+      failures.push(`bucket novo: ${bucket.id}`);
+      continue;
+    }
+    if (bucket.public !== expected.public) {
+      failures.push(`bucket virou ${bucket.public ? 'p√∫blico' : 'privado'}: ${bucket.id}`);
+    }
+    const atual = bucket.file_size_limit ?? null;
+    const esperado = expected.file_size_limit ?? null;
+    if (atual !== esperado) {
+      failures.push(
+        `limite alterado em ${bucket.id}: esperado ${esperado}, atual ${atual}`
+      );
+    }
+  }
+
+  for (const expected of baseline.buckets) {
+    if (!currentById.has(expected.id)) {
+      failures.push(`bucket removido: ${expected.id}`);
+    }
+  }
+
+  return { pass: failures.length === 0, failures };
+}

+import test from 'node:test';
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import { validateStorageBuckets, loadBaseline } from './storage-buckets-baseline.js';
+
+const baseline = loadBaseline();
+
+function makeBucket(id, overrides = {}) {
+  return { id, name: id, public: false, file_size_limit: null, ...overrides };
+}
+
+function currentFromBaseline() {
+  return baseline.buckets.map((b) => ({
+    id: b.id,
+    public: b.public,
+    file_size_limit: b.file_size_limit ?? null,
+  }));
+}
+
+test('validateStorageBuckets: aprova quando tudo confere', () => {
+  const result = validateStorageBuckets(currentFromBaseline(), baseline);
+  assert.equal(result.pass, true);
+  assert.equal(result.failures.length, 0);
+});
+
+test('validateStorageBuckets: reprova bucket novo', () => {
+  const current = [...currentFromBaseline()];
+  current.push(makeBucket('bucket-novo', { public: true }));
+  const result = validateStorageBuckets(current, baseline);
+  assert.equal(result.pass, false);
+  assert.ok(result.failures.some((f) => f.includes('bucket novo')));
+});
+
+test('validateStorageBuckets: reprova bucket que virou publico', () => {
+  const current = baseline.buckets.map((b) => ({
+    id: b.id,
+    public: b.id === 'audio-messages' ? true : b.public,
+    file_size_limit: b.file_size_limit ?? null,
+  }));
+  const result = validateStorageBuckets(current, baseline);
+  assert.equal(result.pass, false);
+  assert.ok(result.failures.some((f) => f.includes('virou p\u00fablico')));
+});
+
+test('validateStorageBuckets: reprova limite alterado', () => {
+  const current = baseline.buckets.map((b) => ({
+    id: b.id,
+    public: b.public,
+    file_size_limit: b.id === 'avatars' ? 1048576 : (b.file_size_limit ?? null),
+  }));
+  const result = validateStorageBuckets(current, baseline);
+  assert.equal(result.pass, false);
+  assert.ok(result.failures.some((f) => f.includes('limite alterado')));
+});
+
+test('validateStorageBuckets: reprova bucket removido', () => {
+  const current = currentFromBaseline().filter((b) => b.id !== 'stickers');
+  const result = validateStorageBuckets(current, baseline);
+  assert.equal(result.pass, false);
+  assert.ok(result.failures.some((f) => f.includes('bucket removido')));
+});

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# N-009 (SEC-DEFINER_GRANTS_STORAGE-06): prova que a migration
+# 20261011003015_storage_limits_stickers_audio_memes.sql restringe os buckets

+# file_size_limit e allowed_mime_types.
+#
+# RED   ‚Äî antes da migration, ambos os buckets tem file_size_limit NULL e
+#         allowed_mime_types NULL (aceitam qualquer MIME, inclusive text/html);
+# GREEN ‚Äî depois da migration, stickers tem file_size_limit=512000 e 4 MIMEs
+#         de imagem (com image/webp); audio-memes tem file_size_limit=5242880
+#         e 5 MIMEs de audio; rollback do cabecalho restaura NULLs e a
+#         reaplicacao volta ao GREEN.
+
+set -Eeuo pipefail
+
+repo_root="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
+migration="$repo_root/supabase/migrations/20261011003015_storage_limits_stickers_audio_memes.sql"
+postgres_image="${STICKERS_MEMES_TEST_POSTGRES_IMAGE:-postgres:17-alpine}"
+container_name="zapp-v2-storage-stickers-memes-test-$$"
+test_password="stickers-memes-test-only"
+
+cleanup() { docker rm -f "$container_name" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; }
+trap cleanup EXIT
+fail() { printf 'FAIL: %s\n' "$1" >&2; exit 1; }
+psql_test() { docker exec -i "$container_name" psql -X -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -U postgres -d postgres "$@"; }
+
+start_postgres() {
+  for attempt in 1 2 3; do
+    docker rm -f "$container_name" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+    if ! docker run -d --name "$container_name" -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD="$test_password" "$postgres_image" >/dev/null; then
+      printf 'WARN: PostgreSQL container failed to start (attempt %s/3)\n' "$attempt" >&2
+      continue
+    fi
+    for _ in $(seq 1 15); do
+      if docker exec "$container_name" psql -X -U postgres -d postgres -Atqc 'SELECT 1' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+        sleep 1
+        if docker exec "$container_name" psql -X -U postgres -d postgres -Atqc 'SELECT 1' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+          return 0
+        fi
+      fi
+      sleep 1
+    done
+    printf 'WARN: PostgreSQL bootstrap was not stable (attempt %s/3)\n' "$attempt" >&2
+    docker logs "$container_name" >&2 || true
+  done
+  return 1
+}
+
+start_postgres || fail 'PostgreSQL de teste nao iniciou'
+
+[[ -f "$migration" ]] || fail "migration ausente: $migration"

+INSERT INTO storage.buckets (id, name, public) VALUES ('stickers', 'stickers', true);
+INSERT INTO storage.buckets (id, name, public) VALUES ('audio-memes', 'audio-memes', true);
+SQL
+
+printf '\n============ BLOCO A ‚Äî estado ANTERIOR (defeito) ============\n'
+
+ST_MIME="$(psql_test -Atqc "SELECT allowed_mime_types IS NULL FROM storage.buckets WHERE id='stickers';")"
+ST_SIZE="$(psql_test -Atqc "SELECT file_size_limit IS NULL FROM storage.buckets WHERE id='stickers';")"
+AM_MIME="$(psql_test -Atqc "SELECT allowed_mime_types IS NULL FROM storage.buckets WHERE id='audio-memes';")"
+AM_SIZE="$(psql_test -Atqc "SELECT file_size_limit IS NULL FROM storage.buckets WHERE id='audio-memes';")"
+ST_PUB="$(psql_test -Atqc "SELECT public FROM storage.buckets WHERE id='stickers';")"

+[[ "$ST_MIME" == 't' ]] || fail "A.1 defeito nao reproduzido: stickers allowed_mime_types deveria ser NULL antes"
+[[ "$ST_SIZE" == 't' ]] || fail "A.2 defeito nao reproduzido: stickers file_size_limit deveria ser NULL antes"
+[[ "$AM_MIME" == 't' ]] || fail "A.3 defeito nao reproduzido: audio-memes allowed_mime_types deveria ser NULL antes"

+printf '[PASS] B.3-B.4 allowed_mime_types exatos nos dois buckets\n'

+psql_test >/dev/null <<'SQL'
+DO $$ BEGIN

+GRANT SELECT ON storage.buckets TO authenticated;

+AUTH_Q() { psql_test -Atqc "SET ROLE authenticated; SELECT $1; RESET ROLE;"; }
+ST_HTML="$(AUTH_Q "'text/html' = ANY (SELECT unnest(allowed_mime_types) FROM storage.buckets WHERE id='stickers')")"

+AM_MPEG="$(AUTH_Q "'audio/mpeg' = ANY (SELECT unnest(allowed_mime_types) FROM storage.buckets WHERE id='audio-memes')")"
+AM_MP4="$(AUTH_Q "'video/mp4' = ANY (SELECT unnest(allowed_mime_types) FROM storage.buckets WHERE id='audio-memes')")"
+[[ "$ST_HTML" == 'f' ]] || fail "B.5 comportamento: 'text/html' = ANY(stickers) deveria ser f (obteve $ST_HTML)"
+[[ "$ST_WEBP" == 't' ]] || fail "B.6 comportamento: 'image/webp' = ANY(stickers) deveria ser t (obteve $ST_WEBP)"
+[[ "$ST_SVG" == 'f' ]] || fail "B.7 comportamento: 'image/svg+xml' = ANY(stickers) deveria ser f (obteve $ST_SVG)"
+[[ "$AM_HTML" == 'f' ]] || fail "B.8 comportamento: 'text/html' = ANY(audio-memes) deveria ser f (obteve $AM_HTML)"
+[[ "$AM_MPEG" == 't' ]] || fail "B.9 comportamento: 'audio/mpeg' = ANY(audio-memes) deveria ser t (obteve $AM_MPEG)"
+[[ "$AM_MP4" == 'f' ]] || fail "B.10 comportamento: 'video/mp4' = ANY(audio-memes) deveria ser f (bucket so de audio, obteve $AM_MP4)"
+printf '[PASS] B.5-B.10 criterio pelo comportamento (ANY) como authenticated: text/html=f nos dois, image/webp=t em stickers, audio/mpeg=t em audio-memes\n'

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# N-010: prova que a migration 20261010130000_storage_limits_whatsapp_audio_multiplix.sql
+# fixa file_size_limit em whatsapp-media, audio-messages e multiplix-voice.
+#
+# RED   ‚Äî sem a migration, os buckets nao tem teto (file_size_limit NULL): um
+#         upload de 30MB passa na checagem (custo sem controle = defeito);
+# GREEN ‚Äî com a migration, o mesmo upload de 30MB e recusado e 1MB passa.
+#
+# BASELINE REAL (ponto 2 da recusa): os buckets nascem nas migrations reais
+#   20251215025014 (audio-messages), 20251223002656 (whatsapp-media) e
+#   20261003132707 F64 (multiplix-voice), e ficam privados na migration real
+#   20260905030000. O teste extrai os INSERTs reais desses arquivos e aplica
+#   a 20260905030000 na integra ‚Äî nada de bucket inventado a mao. Os arquivos
+#   inteiros de seed nao sao aplicaveis isolados: dependem de auth.users e do
+#   schema do Supabase, inexistentes no postgres descartavel.
+#
+# NOTA DE ESCOPO (ponto 1 da recusa): o enforcement real do teto vive na API
+# do Supabase Storage (fora do Postgres): a API le
+# storage.buckets.file_size_limit e recusa o upload acima do teto. No Postgres
+# nao ha trigger nem CHECK que barre o objeto ‚Äî o que a migration entrega e o
+# teto que a API le. A funcao test_upload_gate abaixo (so do teste, nunca da
+# migration) espelha exatamente essa checagem da API (bucket + tamanho ->
+# recusa quando tamanho > limite) para provar o comportamento no banco local.
+
+set -Eeuo pipefail
+
+repo_root="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
+migration="$repo_root/supabase/migrations/20261010130000_storage_limits_whatsapp_audio_multiplix.sql"
+seed_audio="$repo_root/supabase/migrations/20251215025014_fcc5bc79-55e3-4972-8765-6a7840fdce5a.sql"
+seed_wa="$repo_root/supabase/migrations/20251223002656_c427b632-b6ab-4ca4-9b78-38a343925147.sql"
+seed_voice="$repo_root/supabase/migrations/20261003132707_f64_voz_assets_e_grants.sql"
+privatize="$repo_root/supabase/migrations/20260905030000_private_media_buckets.sql"
+postgres_image="${STORAGE_LIMITS_TEST_POSTGRES_IMAGE:-postgres:17-alpine}"
+container_name="zapp-v2-storage-limits-wam-$$"
+test_password="storage_limits_test_only"
+
+cleanup() { docker rm -f "$container_name" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; }
+trap cleanup EXIT
+fail() { printf 'FAIL: %s\n' "$1" >&2; exit 1; }
+psql_test() { docker exec -i "$container_name" psql -X -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -U postgres -d postgres "$@"; }
+psql_sql() { docker exec "$container_name" psql -X -qAt -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -U postgres -d postgres -c "$1" | tail -n1; }
+# Leitura como papel real: a migration roda como dono (owner, como no deploy),
+# e as verificacoes leem como authenticated (papel do app), com claims JWT.
+as_auth() {
+  docker exec "$container_name" psql -X -qAt -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -U postgres -d postgres \
+    -c "SET ROLE authenticated; SET request.jwt.claims TO '{\"sub\":\"00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001\",\"role\":\"authenticated\"}';" \
+    -c "$1" | tail -n1
+}
+expect_value() { # id, sql, esperado (leitura como authenticated)
+  local id="$1" sql="$2" expected="$3" got
+  got="$(as_auth "$sql")"
+  [[ "$got" == "$expected" ]] || fail "$id: esperado [$expected], obtido [$got]"
+  printf '[PASS] %s\n' "$id"
+}
+expect_gate_ok() { # id, bucket, tamanho (upload passa)
+  local id="$1"
+  psql_sql "SELECT test_upload_gate('$2', $3);" >/dev/null \
+    || fail "$id: upload de $3 bytes em $2 deveria passar"
+  printf '[PASS] %s\n' "$id"
+}
+expect_gate_refused() { # id, bucket, tamanho (upload acima do teto recusado)
+  local id="$1" out status
+  set +e
+  out="$(psql_sql "SELECT test_upload_gate('$2', $3);" 2>&1)"
+  status=$?
+  set -e
+  [[ $status -ne 0 ]] || fail "$id: upload de $3 bytes em $2 passou sem teto"
+  [[ "$out" == *"object too large"* ]] || fail "$id: recusa sem mensagem de teto (saida: $out)"
+  printf '[PASS] %s\n' "$id"
+}
+# Extrai de um arquivo de migration real o statement INSERT que cria o bucket.
+extract_bucket_insert() { # arquivo, bucket
+  awk -v b="$2" '
+    /^INSERT INTO storage\.buckets/ { buf=""; active=1 }
+    active { buf = buf $0 "\n" }
+    active && /;/ { if (buf ~ b) printf "%s", buf; active=0; buf="" }
+  ' "$1"
+}
+
+command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail 'docker indisponivel'
+docker info >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail 'daemon docker indisponivel'
+[[ -f "$migration" ]] || fail "migration nao encontrada: $migration"
+[[ -f "$seed_audio" ]] || fail "seed real nao encontrada: $seed_audio"
+[[ -f "$seed_wa" ]] || fail "seed real nao encontrada: $seed_wa"
+[[ -f "$seed_voice" ]] || fail "seed real nao encontrada: $seed_voice"
+[[ -f "$privatize" ]] || fail "migration real nao encontrada: $privatize"
+
+if ! docker run -d --rm --name "$container_name" \
+  -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD="$test_password" \
+  "$postgres_image" >/dev/null; then
+  fail 'PostgreSQL de teste nao iniciou'
+fi
+ready=0
+for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
+  if docker exec "$container_name" pg_isready -U postgres >/dev/null 2>&1; then ready=1; break; fi
+  sleep 1
+done
+[[ "$ready" == "1" ]] || fail 'PostgreSQL de teste nao iniciou'
+
+# Infraestrutura real do Supabase: o schema storage e a tabela buckets existem
+# no servidor e nenhuma migration os cria. O teste declara a tabela no formato
+# real (colunas usadas pelos INSERTs reais do repo: id text, name, public,
+# file_size_limit, allowed_mime_types).
+psql_test -q <<'SQL' >/dev/null
+CREATE SCHEMA storage;
+CREATE TABLE storage.buckets (
+  id text PRIMARY KEY,
+  name text UNIQUE NOT NULL,
+  public boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
+  file_size_limit bigint,
+  allowed_mime_types text[]
+);
+DO $$ BEGIN
+  IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = 'authenticated') THEN
+    CREATE ROLE authenticated;
+  END IF;
+END $$;
+GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA storage TO authenticated;
+GRANT SELECT ON storage.buckets TO authenticated;
+GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public TO authenticated;
+SQL
+
+# Gate de upload (somente teste): espelha a checagem que a API do Supabase
+# Storage faz antes de aceitar o objeto ‚Äî tamanho > file_size_limit recusa;
+# limite NULL significa sem teto (qualquer tamanho passa = defeito).
+psql_test -q <<'SQL' >/dev/null
+CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.test_upload_gate(p_bucket text, p_size bigint)
+RETURNS void LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $fn$
+DECLARE v_limit bigint;
+BEGIN
+  SELECT file_size_limit INTO v_limit FROM storage.buckets WHERE name = p_bucket;
+  IF NOT FOUND THEN
+    RAISE EXCEPTION 'bucket not found: %', p_bucket;
+  END IF;
+  IF v_limit IS NULL THEN RETURN; END IF;
+  IF p_size > v_limit THEN
+    RAISE EXCEPTION 'object too large: % bytes exceeds bucket % limit of % bytes', p_size, p_bucket, v_limit;
+  END IF;
+END $fn$;
+SQL
+
+echo ''
+echo '============ BLOCO A ‚Äî baseline real (defeito) ============'
+# Cria os tres buckets com os INSERTs REAIS extraidos das migrations de seed.
+for spec in "$seed_audio audio-messages" "$seed_wa whatsapp-media" "$seed_voice multiplix-voice"; do
+  set -- $spec
+  stmt="$(extract_bucket_insert "$1" "$2")"
+  [[ -n "$stmt" ]] || fail "A.0 INSERT real de $2 nao extraido de ${1##*/}"
+  [[ "$stmt" == *"storage.buckets"* && "$stmt" == *"$2"* ]] \
+    || fail "A.0 extracao invalida para $2"
+  printf '%s\n' "$stmt" | psql_test -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -q >/dev/null \
+    || fail "A.0 INSERT real de $2 falhou"
+  printf '[PASS] A.0 bucket %s criado pelo INSERT real de %s\n' "$2" "${1##*/}"
+done
+expect_value 'A.1 whatsapp-media sem file_size_limit (baseline real)' \
+  "SELECT file_size_limit IS NULL FROM storage.buckets WHERE name='whatsapp-media';" 't'
+expect_value 'A.2 audio-messages sem file_size_limit (baseline real)' \
+  "SELECT file_size_limit IS NULL FROM storage.buckets WHERE name='audio-messages';" 't'
+expect_value 'A.3 multiplix-voice sem file_size_limit (baseline real)' \
+  "SELECT file_size_limit IS NULL FROM storage.buckets WHERE name='multiplix-voice';" 't'
+expect_value 'A.4 whatsapp-media nasce public=true na seed real' \
+  "SELECT public FROM storage.buckets WHERE name='whatsapp-media';" 't'
+# Migration real que fecha os buckets com dados de clientes (aplica na integra:
+# e um unico UPDATE, sem dependencias).
+psql_test -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -q < "$privatize" >/dev/null \
+  || fail 'A.5 migration real 20260905030000 falhou'

@@ -0,0 +1,322 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# N-103 Talk X: pesos das variantes somam 100 e atribuicao est√°vel.
+#
+# Contrato num PostgreSQL 17 descartavel, no mesmo formato dos testes irmaos
+# (scripts/db-audit/talkx-audience-snapshot.test.sh, scripts/db-audit/talkx-role-gates.test.sh).
+#
+# Aplica a migration N-103 REAL (supabase/migrations/*_talkx_ab_weights_constraint.sql)
+# sobre um schema minimo com a tabela talkx_template_variants, e prova:
+#   (a) migration aplica e e replayavel; trigger e functions existem;
+#       e a migration NAO carrega DDL de colunas A/B (escopo da constraint);
+#   (b) INSERT com pesos validos (soma=100) ‚Äî aceito;
+#   (c) INSERT com pesos invalidos (60+40+30=130) ‚Äî rejeitado com SQLSTATE 22023;
+#   (d) UPDATE que quebra a soma ‚Äî rejeitado com SQLSTATE 22023;
+#   (e) UPDATE que mantem a soma ‚Äî aceito;
+#   (f) DELETE que quebra a soma ‚Äî rejeitado com SQLSTATE 22023;
+#   (g) DELETE que deixa o template vazio ‚Äî aceito, e assign_variant em template
+#       vazio levanta 22023 (sem fallback silencioso);
+#   (h) troca de template_id: rejeitada quando o template antigo deixa de somar 100,
+#       aceita quando ambos ficam em 100;
+#   (i) talkx_assign_variant: o mesmo contato recebe a mesma variante em 2 snapshots;
+#   (j) contatos distintos respeitam os pesos (distribuicao A=60 / B=40);
+#   (k) authenticated nao executa talkx_assign_variant (grant so para service_role);
+#   (l) escopo: a migration nao carrega DDL das colunas A/B (ab_*) em talkx_campaigns.
+
+set -euo pipefail
+
+repo_root=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)
+# TALKX_AB_WEIGHTS_MIGRATION permite a prova vermelho-verde: rodar ESTE teste
+# contra a migration anterior (que falha) e contra a migration atual (que passa).
+if [[ -n "${TALKX_AB_WEIGHTS_MIGRATION:-}" ]]; then
+  migration_n103="$TALKX_AB_WEIGHTS_MIGRATION"
+else
+  mapfile -t migration_candidates < <(ls -1 "$repo_root"/supabase/migrations/*_talkx_ab_weights_constraint.sql 2>/dev/null || true)
+  [[ "${#migration_candidates[@]}" == '1' ]] \
+    || { printf 'FAIL: esperava exatamente 1 migration talkx_ab_weights_constraint, achei %s\n' "${#migration_candidates[@]}" >&2; exit 1; }
+  migration_n103="${migration_candidates[0]}"
+fi
+postgres_image="${TALKX_AB_WEIGHTS_TEST_POSTGRES_IMAGE:-postgres:17-alpine}"
+container_name="talkx-ab-weights-test-$$"
+test_password="talkx_ab_weights_test_only"
+
+cleanup() { docker rm -f "$container_name" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; }
+trap cleanup EXIT
+fail() { printf 'FAIL: %s\n' "$1" >&2; exit 1; }
+pass() { printf 'PASS: %s\n' "$1"; }
+psql_test() { docker exec -i "$container_name" psql -X -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -U postgres -d postgres "$@"; }
+psql_q() { psql_test -Atqc "$1"; }
+
+expect_error() {
+  local label="$1" message="$2" errcode="$3" sql="$4" out status
+  set +e
+  out="$(psql_test -v VERBOSITY=verbose -c "$sql" 2>&1)"
+  status=$?
+  set -e
+  (( status != 0 )) || { printf '%s\n' "$out" >&2; fail "$label: deveria falhar, mas passou"; }
+  [[ "$out" == *"$message"* ]] || { printf '%s\n' "$out" >&2; fail "$label: esperava a mensagem '$message'"; }
+  [[ "$out" == *"$errcode"* ]] || { printf '%s\n' "$out" >&2; fail "$label: esperava o SQLSTATE '$errcode'"; }
+  pass "$label"
+}
+
+start_postgres() {
+  for attempt in 1 2 3; do
+    docker rm -f "$container_name" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+    if ! docker run -d --name "$container_name" -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD="$test_password" "$postgres_image" >/dev/null; then
+      printf 'WARN: PostgreSQL container failed to start (attempt %s/3)\n' "$attempt" >&2
+      continue
+    fi
+    for _ in $(seq 1 15); do
+      if docker exec "$container_name" psql -X -U postgres -d postgres -Atqc 'SELECT 1' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+        sleep 1
+        if docker exec "$container_name" psql -X -U postgres -d postgres -Atqc 'SELECT 1' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+          return 0
+        fi
+      fi
+      sleep 1
+    done
+    printf 'WARN: PostgreSQL bootstrap was not stable (attempt %s/3)\n' "$attempt" >&2
+    docker ps -a --filter "name=^/${container_name}$" --format 'talkx-test-container {{.Status}}' >&2 || true
+    docker logs "$container_name" >&2 || true
+  done
+  return 1
+}
+
+start_postgres || fail 'PostgreSQL de teste nao iniciou'
+

+assert_eq() {
+  local label="$1" expected="$2" actual="$3"
+  [[ "$actual" == "$expected" ]] || fail "$label: esperado '$expected', obtido '$actual'"
+  pass "$label (= $actual)"
+}
+# Confere um par chave/valor do jsonb sem depender da ordem das chaves.
+assert_field() {
+  local label="$1" key="$2" expected="$3" json="$4"
+  [[ "$json" == *"\"$key\": $expected"* || "$json" == *"\"$key\":$expected"* ]] \
+    || fail "$label: campo '$key' esperado '$expected' em -> $json"
+  pass "$label ($key = $expected)"
+}
+assert_fails_like() {

+  set +e
+  out="$(docker exec "$pg_name" psql -X -Atq -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -U postgres -d postgres -c "$sql" 2>&1)"
+  status=$?
+  set -e
+  (( status != 0 )) || fail "$label: deveria falhar, passou"
+  [[ "$out" == *"$pattern"* ]] || fail "$label: erro inesperado -> $out"
+  pass "$label ($pattern)"

+DECLARE
+  v_max_value     numeric;
+  v_id            uuid;
+BEGIN
+  IF auth.role() IS DISTINCT FROM 'service_role' THEN
+    RAISE EXCEPTION 'talkx_conversion_service_role_only' USING ERRCODE = '42501';

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Harness descartavel: N-123 / X075 ‚Äî talkx_benchmarks(p_days, p_limit) com nomes.
+# Prova: a assinatura antiga sem argumentos e removida; a nova devolve nome de segmento
+# (so para admin/supervisor) e de template, volume enviado (sent_count), templates
+# ordenados por taxa de resposta e has_baseline (true com 5+ campanhas concluidas na
+# janela). Aplica os ARQUIVOS de migration reais num PostgreSQL 17 descartavel e roda
+# como o papel real (SET LOCAL ROLE authenticated), nunca como postgres no caminho feliz.
+set -euo pipefail
+
+repo_root="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
+fail() { printf '[FAIL] %s\n' "$1" >&2; exit 1; }
+psql_test() { docker exec -i "$cid" psql -X -q -v ON_ERROR_STOP=0 -U postgres -d postgres "$@"; }
+psql_q() { psql_test -Atqc "$1"; }
+
+test_password='talkx_benchmarks_test_only'
+cid="talkx-benchmarks-$RANDOM$RANDOM"
+cleanup() { if [[ "$cid" =~ ^talkx-benchmarks-[0-9]+$ ]]; then docker rm -f "$cid" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; fi; }
+trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM
+
+command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail 'Docker nao esta instalado'
+docker info >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail 'Docker daemon nao acessivel'
+docker run --rm -d --name "$cid" -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD="$test_password" postgres:17-alpine >/dev/null
+
+ready=false
+for _ in $(seq 1 90); do
+  markers="$(docker logs "$cid" 2>&1 | grep -c 'database system is ready to accept connections' || true)"
+  if [[ "$markers" -ge 2 ]] && docker exec "$cid" psql -X -U postgres -d postgres -Atqc 'SELECT 1' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    ready=true; break
+  fi
+  sleep 1
+done
+[[ "$ready" == true ]] || fail 'PostgreSQL 17 descartavel nao ficou pronto'
+

+psql_test >/dev/null <<'SQL'

+$$;
+CREATE FUNCTION auth.role() RETURNS text LANGUAGE sql STABLE AS $$
+  SELECT NULLIF(current_setting('request.jwt.claim.role', true), '')::text
+$$;
+CREATE ROLE service_role NOLOGIN;
+CREATE ROLE authenticated NOLOGIN;
+CREATE ROLE anon NOLOGIN;
+

+  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# N-107 Talk X banco: lista de bloqueio guarda trilha e nao apaga linha.
+#
+# Prova comportamental (banco descartavel PG17, papel real via SET ROLE +
+# request.jwt.claim.sub):
+#  1. INSERT com blocked_by forjado e clamped pelo trigger para o perfil do
+#     chamador (lookup profiles.user_id = auth.uid()); backend sem claim
+#     (service_role) mantem o valor informado.
+#  2. UPDATE que preenche removed_at com removed_by forjado e clamped para o
+#     perfil do chamador; reativacao (removed_at = NULL) mantem NULLs.
+#  2b. Linha ja removida que continua removida preserva removed_by/removed_at
+#     (edicao de outro admin nao troca o autor); UPDATE autenticado nunca
+#     reescreve blocked_by.
+#  3. DELETE fisico recusado com a mensagem da trigger para authenticated
+#     admin (policy permitiria) E para service_role (fora do RLS).
+#  4. Colunas novas import_batch_id/removal_reason gravam e leem.
+#  5. REVOKE: nenhuma das funcoes novas e executavel por PUBLIC/anon/
+#     authenticated (o trigger dispara mesmo assim ‚Äî provado pelos itens 1-3).
+#  6. Rollback da linha 2 da migration executa e restaura o estado anterior;
+#     reaplicar a migration volta a funcionar.
+#
+# O schema vem das MIGRATIONS REAIS de talkx_blacklist (falha dura se algum
+# arquivo sumir ‚Äî sem pulo condicional silencioso). Harness sintetico existe SO
+# para dependencias de outras tabelas (auth mock, papeis, stubs profiles/
+# contacts/messages com as PKs referenciadas) e para blocos canonicos que nao
+# sao aplicaveis standalone (cada um rotulado HARNESS com a fonte canonica).
+set -euo pipefail
+
+REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
+MIG_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/supabase/migrations"
+
+# --- migrations reais de talkx_blacklist (ordem do ledger) --------------------
+F_CREATE="$MIG_DIR/20260409013057_7a6fb7ad-d6f8-4517-a461-ef10c0123af1.sql"
+F_AUDIT="$MIG_DIR/20260910080000_talkx_blacklist_audit.sql"
+F_V2="$MIG_DIR/20260910090000_talkx_blacklist_v2.sql"
+F_UPDATE_POL="$MIG_DIR/20260910100000_restrict_talkx_blacklist_update_policy.sql"
+F_V05="$MIG_DIR/20260929860000_talkx_blacklist_origin_check_and_phone_active_unique.sql"
+F_V07="$MIG_DIR/20260930160000_talkx_blacklist_contact_active_unique.sql"
+F_PHONE_AXIS="$MIG_DIR/20260930330000_talkx_suppress_contact_phone_axis.sql"
+F_NEW="$MIG_DIR/20261011003007_talkx_blacklist_audit_trilha_guarda.sql"
+
+fail() { echo "[FAIL] $*" >&2; exit 1; }
+ok()   { echo "[OK] $*"; }
+
+# Sem pulo silencioso: cada arquivo real precisa existir (falha dura).
+for f in "$F_CREATE" "$F_AUDIT" "$F_V2" "$F_UPDATE_POL" "$F_V05" "$F_V07" "$F_PHONE_AXIS" "$F_NEW"; do
+  [[ -f "$f" ]] || fail "migration real ausente: $f"
+done
+# O espelho comentado (--   stmt;) precisa ser identico ao SQL da linha 2.
+RB_LINE2=$(sed -n 's/^-- Rollback: //p' "$F_NEW")
+[[ -n "$RB_LINE2" ]] || fail "linha 2 da migration nova nao e -- Rollback: com SQL"
+grep -q '^-- Rollback (SQL execut' "$F_NEW" || fail "migration nova sem bloco -- Rollback (SQL executavel)"
+while IFS= read -r stmt; do
+  body="${stmt#--   }"
+  [[ "$body" == *";" ]] || fail "linha de rollback sem ponto-e-virgula: $stmt"
+  [[ "$RB_LINE2" == *"$body"* ]] || fail "rollback comentado diverge da linha 2: $stmt"
+done < <(grep '^--   [^ ]' "$F_NEW")
+[[ "$(grep -c '^--   [^ ]' "$F_NEW")" == "7" ]] || fail "espelho do rollback incompleto"
+echo "[OK] rollback da linha 2 e espelho comentado conferem (7 comandos)"
+ok "migrations reais presentes (create, audit, v2, update-policy, V05, V07, phone-axis, N-107)"

+# --- postgres descartavel ------------------------------------------------------
+IMAGE="${TALKX_BLACKLIST_AUDIT_TEST_POSTGRES_IMAGE:-pgvector/pgvector:0.8.0-pg17}"
+CID="talkx-blacklist-audit-test-$$"
+docker rm -f "$CID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+docker run -d --name "$CID" -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres "$IMAGE" >/dev/null \
+  || fail "subir postgres descartavel ($IMAGE)"
+trap 'docker rm -f "$CID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true' EXIT
+ready=false
+for _ in $(seq 1 120); do
+  if docker exec "$CID" pg_isready -U postgres >/dev/null 2>&1; then ready=true; break; fi
+  sleep 1
+done
+if [[ "$ready" != true ]]; then
+  docker logs "$CID" 2>&1 | tail -n 20 >&2 || true
+  fail "postgres descartavel nao ficou pronto"
+fi
+# O entrypoint reinicia o postgres apos o setup inicial (pg_isready pode
+# acertar o servidor temporario); espera estabilizar antes do primeiro psql.
+sleep 5
+ready=false
+for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
+  if docker exec "$CID" pg_isready -U postgres >/dev/null 2>&1; then ready=true; break; fi
+  sleep 1
+done
+[[ "$ready" == true ]] || fail "postgres descartavel caiu apos o setup inicial"
+
+PSQL=(docker exec -i "$CID" psql -U postgres -d postgres -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -q -t -A)
+PSQL_NO_STOP=(docker exec -i "$CID" psql -U postgres -d postgres -v ON_ERROR_STOP=0 -q -t -A)
+apply() { # apply <arquivo>: aplica migration real, falha em qualquer erro
+  "${PSQL[@]}" < "$1" >/dev/null || fail "aplicar migration real: $1"
+  echo "[OK] aplicada: $(basename "$1")"
+}
+run() { # run <sql...>: executa e imprime stdout
+  "${PSQL[@]}" -c "$*"
